messages:
mira: Heads-up — customer on Cloudflare Workers hit a TS + runtime issue with the JS SDK. They import the package in an edge function and get two errors: runtime `ReferenceError: require is not defined` and a TS error `No matching overload` for `client.chat.create<T>(...)`. Any quick workarounds?

sam: Edge needs ESM — are they using `require()` anywhere? The SDK currently ships a CJS entry point + an ESM build, but our `exports` map might be resolving to the CJS one for some bundlers.

mira: They're using `import { Client } from '@redwood/inference'` (ESM syntax). TSC still complains about overloads. The runtime `require` error comes from one of our dev-deps being pulled into the bundle? Hard to trace.

jon: For the TS part: overloads can break generic inference. If we have multiple signatures for `create` (chat completion, streaming, tools) TS sometimes can't pick the right one. Could be the combination of `unknown` in params + overloads causing inference to fail.

lee: Workarounds: 1) have them set `compilerOptions.module: "esnext"` and `moduleResolution: "bundler"` in their `tsconfig` so the bundler/tsc resolve ESM patterns better. 2) set `skipLibCheck: true` to bypass our d.ts strictness temporarily. But both are meh as long-term fixes.

mira: Example tsconfig they tried (we suggested):
```json
{
  "compilerOptions": {
    "target": "es2020",
    "module": "esnext",
    "moduleResolution": "bundler",
    "skipLibCheck": true
  }
}
```

sam: For runtime: we should ensure `package.json` exports prefer `./dist/edge/index.mjs` for `import` in edge environments. Something like: 
```json
"exports": {
  ".": {
    "import": "./dist/esm/index.mjs",
    "require": "./dist/cjs/index.js"
  },
  "./edge/": {
    "import": "./dist/edge/index.mjs",
    "types": "./dist/edge/index.d.ts"
  }
}
```

lee: Agreed. Also want a smaller edge bundle that excludes Node-only internals (fs, child_process) and picks only edge-friendly polyfills. We'll add an edge rollup target.

mira: About the TS overloads — customer dev said they had to cast to `any` to make generics flow. That defeats the safety goal.

jon: We should avoid overloading public API in the ways TS cannot infer. Suggest replacing multiple overloads with a single generic signature and narrow at runtime. E.g. `create<T extends ResponseShape = Default>(opts: CreateOpts): Promise<T>` and internal discriminated unions for behavior. That usually plays nicer with TS type inference.

lee: On `unknown` vs `any`: we used `unknown` for the `input`/`metadata` fields to force explicit validation. But this is biting DX. Option: keep `unknown` in internal types, but expose looser `any` in the public convenience overloads where inference matters, or provide helper typed wrappers in our SDK.

mira: Can we ship a quick patch that: 1) adds an `./edge` export, 2) publishes an edge-optimized ESM build, and 3) loosens the typings for `create` to a single generic signature? Customer needs a short-term fix.

lee: I can draft a PR with the bundler config + exports + simplified typing changes. Will also add a short migration note to the sample Cloudflare Worker app showing the recommended `tsconfig` and import.

sam: Please also add a small test that bundles the worker sample with `wrangler` and `esbuild` to catch regressions.

ci-bot: Created issue #412: "edge esm export + typing ergonomics for create APIs" https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/issues/412 (assigned to @lee)

mira: Awesome — I'll let the customer know we have a fix coming. For internal tracking, can we add a short blurb to the onboarding sample apps so new users don't hit this?

lee: Yes — I'll update `examples/worker/*` with the new tsconfig snippet + import example and a note: "If you see `require is not defined`, ensure you're using the edge build (see exports)."

jon: +1 on the typing change. We should also document why we prefer `unknown` and where we relax to `any` so reviewers know it's deliberate.

sam: Thanks all. If anyone sees other edge compatibility bugs please drop them in #devex. :thumbsup:

mira: Thanks — will follow up once the PR lands. :rocket:
